chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into Ihram for Hajj during months other than the months of Hajj, before the specific time designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He (peace be upon him) said: 'His Ihram is not [invalidated] by anything. If he wishes to return to his house, let him return, and I do not see any blame upon him. And if he wishes to continue, let him continue. So when he reaches the proper time, let him enter into Ihram from there and make it an Umrah, for that is superior to his returning, because he has publicly announced the Ihram for Hajj.'

key_terms.أشهر الحج: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qi'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, and part of Rajab)
key_terms.إحرام: Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who enters Ihram for Hajj before the correct time or in a non-Hajj month?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the flexibility in Hajj jurisprudence, distinguishing between the validity of the state of Ihram and the timing of the specific ritual obligations. It establishes that performing Hajj outside the canonical months (Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and part of Muharram) is permissible, with the option to convert the early Ihram into an Umrah, thereby maximizing spiritual reward by publicly declaring the intention. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the continuity of worship and the validity of intentions even when temporal conditions are not strictly met.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who wore Ihraam for Hajj during other than the months of the Hajj, besides the juncture which Rasool-Allahsaww had designated’. Heasws said: ‘His Ihraam is not with anything. If he so likes to, he can return to his house, so let him return, and Iasws do not see anything upon him; and if keeps going, so let him keep going. So when he ends up to a juncture, so let him wear Ihraam from it, and make it to be an Umra, for that would be superior than his returning, because he announced the Ihraam to be for the Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who assumes the state of Ihram for al- Hajj. He does it in a month, which is other than the months of al-Hajj. It is at a place other than those designated by the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. He (the Imam) said, ‘His Ihram is not valid. If he likes, he can go to his home; and I do not see anything against him, or to continue and upon arriving at Miqat (place for assuming the state of Ihram), assume the state of Ihram at that point, and make it an al-‘Umrah. It is more virtuous than his returning home when he has already announced his state of Ihram for al- Hajj.’”
